name: Jephunneh
description: Caleb's father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes.

The tenth provocation was the report of the spies, and it was the last: how long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, because Caleb had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

points: The Lord heard their words and was wroth and sware: not one of the men of that evil generation would see the good land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, because he wholly followed the Lord, and Joshua the son of Nun, who would cause Israel to inherit it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

points: Joshua blessed him and gave Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance, and it became his inheritance unto this day, because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

points: Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua, even the city of Arba, which is Hebron.

note.label: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

points: Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.
